quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a confident opening at an interview.
quests.hint: 'thank you for' links as 'thank-yuh-fuh'; the peaks are SEEing, toDAY, LOOKing, FORward and INterview.
quests.explanation: A warm opener uses a light, quick 'thank you for' and a clear peak on the key words. 'interview' stresses the first syllable, and 'forward' ends with a clear [d].
quests.textToSpeak: Thank you for seeing me today; I've been looking forward to this interview.
quests.phoneticHint: [ˈθæŋk jə fə ˈsiːɪŋ mi təˈdeɪ] | [aɪv bɪn ˈlʊkɪŋ ˈfɔːrwərd tə ðɪs ˈɪntərvjuː].
commonMistakes: Saying 'thank you for' as three heavy words

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a summary of experience.
quests.hint: 'logistics' stresses JIS, 'coordinating' stresses OR, 'deliveries' stresses LIV, and 'regions' stresses REE.
quests.explanation: Professional words need a clear stressed syllable. 'six' ends in [ks] and 'three' starts with [θr], so give them a moment.
quests.textToSpeak: I've worked in logistics for six years, mostly coordinating deliveries across three regions.
quests.phoneticHint: 'logistics' is [ləˈdʒɪstɪks], 'coordinating' is [koʊˈɔːrdɪneɪtɪŋ], 'deliveries' is [dɪˈlɪvəriz], and 'regions' is [ˈriːdʒənz].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as you would state an achievement.
quests.hint: Peaks on CURrent, MANage, EIGHT, reDUCED, THIRty and perCENT. 'thirty' and 'percent' are the key figures.
quests.explanation: Numbers carry the message in an achievement statement. Say 'thirty' with stress on the first syllable and 'percent' with stress on the second.
quests.textToSpeak: In my current role, I manage a team of eight, and we reduced errors by thirty percent last year.
quests.phoneticHint: [ɪn maɪ ˈkɜːrənt ˈroʊl aɪ ˈmænɪdʒ ə ˈtiːm əv ˈeɪt ənd wi rɪˈdjuːst ˈerərz baɪ ˈθɜːrti pərˈsent ˈlæst ˈjɪr].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as an interview answer Watch the interview strengths: [ŋθ] and stress.
quests.hint: 'strength' ends in [ŋθ], 'problem-solving' has stress on PROB and SOLV, and 'practical' stresses PRAC.
quests.explanation: 'strength' starts with [str] and ends with [ŋθ]: keep the tongue at the teeth to finish. Stress the key nouns to sell your point.
quests.textToSpeak: My greatest strength is problem-solving; I stay calm and look for practical solutions.
quests.phoneticHint: 'strength' is [streŋθ], 'practical' is [ˈpræktɪkəl], and 'solutions' is [səˈluːʃənz].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as an honest interview answer.
quests.hint: 'honest' has a silent h, 'weakness' stresses WEAK, and 'prioritise' stresses OR.
quests.explanation: A softener like 'if I'm honest' is light and quick, then the content is clear. 'prioritise' has four syllables with the stress on the second: pri-OR-i-tize.
quests.textToSpeak: If I'm honest, my weakness is that I sometimes take on too much, but I'm learning to prioritise.
quests.phoneticHint: [ɪf aɪm ˈɒnɪst maɪ ˈwiːknəs ɪz ðət aɪ ˈsʌmtaɪmz ˈteɪk ˈɒn ˈtuː ˈmʌtʃ bət aɪm ˈlɜːrnɪŋ tə praɪˈɒrɪtaɪz].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a question at the end of an interview.
quests.hint: A rising tone on 'team' and a fall on 'like'; 'typical' stresses TYP.
quests.explanation: A polite question at the end of an interview: keep 'could you tell me' light, use a small rise after 'team', and finish with a gentle fall.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you tell me more about the team, and what a typical week would look like?
quests.phoneticHint: [ˈkʊdʒə ˈtel mi ˈmɔːr əˈbaʊt ðə ˈtiːm] | [ənd wɒt ə ˈtɪpɪkəl ˈwiːk wʊd ˈlʊk ˈlaɪk].
commonMistakes: Saying 'typical' with the stress on the second syllable
Rising at the end of the whole sentence

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a quick workplace update.
quests.hint: 'confirmed' ends in [md], 'vendor' stresses VEN, and 'shipment' stresses SHIP.
quests.explanation: A quick update is rhythmic: short opener, then clear facts. 'confirmed' has two syllables (con-FIRMD) and ends with [md].
quests.textToSpeak: Quick update: the vendor confirmed the shipment for Tuesday, so we're still on schedule.
quests.phoneticHint: [ˈkwɪk ˈʌpdeɪt] | [ðə ˈvendər kənˈfɜːrmd ðə ˈʃɪpmənt fər ˈtuːzdeɪ] | [soʊ wɪr ˈstɪl ɒn ˈʃedjuːl].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a status report.
quests.hint: 'analysis' stresses NAL, 'summary' stresses SUM, and 'department' stresses PART.
quests.explanation: In a status update, the peaks fall on the actions and the outcomes: FINished, aNALysis, SENT, SUMmary. Keep 'this morning' and 'to everyone' light.
quests.textToSpeak: I finished the analysis this morning, and I've sent the summary to everyone in the department.
quests.targetPhoneme: work update: stress in long words
quests.phoneticHint: [aɪ ˈfɪnɪʃt ði əˈnæləsɪs ðɪs ˈmɔːrnɪŋ] | [ənd aɪv ˈsent ðə ˈsʌməri tə ˈevriwʌn ɪn ðə dɪˈpɑːrtmənt].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a team update.
quests.hint: 'couple of' becomes 'coupla', 'issues' stresses IS, and 'developers' stresses VEL.
quests.explanation: This sentence has a contrast: problem, then solution. Use a small fall-rise on 'software', then a firm fall on 'one'.
quests.textToSpeak: We ran into a couple of issues with the software, but the developers have already fixed the main one.
quests.phoneticHint: [wi ˈræn ˈɪntu ə ˈkʌplə əv ˈɪʃuːz wɪð ðə ˈsɒftweər] | [bət ðə dɪˈveləpərz həv ɔːlˈredi ˈfɪkst ðə ˈmeɪn ˈwʌn].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a polite request to a colleague.
quests.hint: 'Would you be able to' becomes 'wouldja be able ta', and 'review' is re-VIEW.
quests.explanation: Polite requests use light small words and a gentle rise on the request. Keep 'I'd really appreciate' warm, with a higher pitch on 'really'.
quests.textToSpeak: Would you be able to review this document before lunch? I'd really appreciate a second opinion.
quests.phoneticHint: [ˈwʊdʒə bi ˈeɪbəl tə rɪˈvjuː ðɪs ˈdɒkjumənt bɪˈfɔːr ˈlʌntʃ] | [aɪd ˈrɪəli əˈpriːʃieɪt ə ˈsekənd əˈpɪnjən].
commonMistakes: Stressing 'would you be able to' strongly
Falling sharply on 'lunch', which sounds like a command

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a request during a busy day.
quests.hint: 'take over' links as 'ta-kover', 'technical' stresses TECH, and 'while I' links.
quests.explanation: The request is long, so chunk it: 'Could you take over the presentation' | 'while I deal with the technical problem'.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you take over the presentation while I deal with the technical problem?
quests.phoneticHint: [kʊdʒə ˈteɪk oʊvər ðə ˌprezənˈteɪʃən] | [waɪl aɪ ˈdiːl wɪð ðə ˈteknɪkəl ˈprɒbləm].
commonMistakes: Not pausing between the two chunks

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as an indirect request.
quests.hint: 'swamped' ends in [mpt], 'wondering' stresses WON, and 'whether you could' runs together.
quests.explanation: This is an indirect request: soft opener, reason, then request. Use a small rise on 'week', and finish with a gentle fall on 'workshop'.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm swamped this week, so I was wondering whether you could handle the booking for the workshop.
quests.phoneticHint: [aɪm ˈswɒmpt ðɪs ˈwiːk soʊ aɪ wəz ˈwʌndərɪŋ ˈweðər jə kʊd ˈhændəl ðə ˈbʊkɪŋ fə ðə ˈwɜːrkʃɒp].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as you would open a meeting.
quests.hint: 'Shall we' starts with [ʃ], 'get started' links, and 'going through' links.
quests.explanation: A meeting opener is short and confident: a rising 'Shall we get started?' then a falling statement.
quests.textToSpeak: Shall we get started? Let's begin by going through the agenda.
quests.phoneticHint: [ʃəl wi ˈget ˈstɑːrtɪd] rising | [lets bɪˈgɪn baɪ ˈgoʊɪŋ θruː ði əˈdʒendə] falling.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a friendly meeting opener.
quests.hint: 'a lot to cover' becomes 'a lotta cover', and 'brief' ends with [f].
quests.explanation: Greeting the group uses a warm, friendly tone. 'everyone' is three syllables (EV-ree-wun) and 'brief' ends in a clean [f].
quests.textToSpeak: Thanks, everyone, for making the time; we've got a lot to cover, so I'll keep this brief.
quests.phoneticHint: [ˈθæŋks ˈevriwʌn fə ˈmeɪkɪŋ ðə ˈtaɪm] | [wɪv ˈgɒt ə ˈlɒtə ˈkʌvər soʊ aɪl ˈkiːp ðɪs ˈbriːf].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as an agenda.
quests.hint: 'followed' ends in [d], 'staffing' has [f], and 'business' has two syllables.
quests.explanation: An agenda is a list: rise slightly after each item and fall at the end. 'followed by' links as 'follow-dby'.
quests.textToSpeak: The first item is the budget, followed by staffing, and then we'll finish with any other business.
quests.phoneticHint: [ðə ˈfɜːrst ˈaɪtəm ɪz ðə ˈbʌdʒɪt] | [ˈfɒloʊd baɪ ˈstæfɪŋ] | [ənd ðen wiːl ˈfɪnɪʃ wɪð ˈeni ˈʌðər ˈbɪznəs].
commonMistakes: Pronouncing the 'i' in 'business' as a full vowel
Ending each agenda item with a full fall

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a polite disagreement.
quests.hint: 'point' has a fall-rise, and 'work' has the main peak; 'in practice' falls.
quests.explanation: A fall-rise on 'point' signals that a 'but' follows. The disagreement itself is softened with 'I'm not sure'.
quests.textToSpeak: I see your point, but I'm not sure that would work in practice.
quests.phoneticHint: [aɪ ˈsiː jər ˈpɔɪnt] fall-rise | [bət aɪm ˈnɒt ˈʃʊr ðət wʊd ˈwɜːrk ɪn ˈpræktɪs] fall.
commonMistakes: Falling firmly on 'point', which sounds like full agreement
Saying 'practice' with stress on the second syllable

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as you would seek clarification.
quests.hint: 'exactly' is ig-ZAKT-ly, 'flexible' stresses FLEX, and 'on the same page' is a chunk.
quests.explanation: A clarifying question uses a rise on the key word 'flexible'. The follow-up sentence explains why you're asking, in a lower pitch.
quests.textToSpeak: What exactly do you mean by 'flexible'? I want to make sure we're on the same page.
quests.targetPhoneme: clarifying: rise on the key word
quests.phoneticHint: [ˈwɒt ɪgˈzæktli də ju ˈmiːn baɪ ˈfleksɪbəl] | [aɪ ˈwɒnə ˈmeɪk ˈʃʊr wɪr ɒn ðə ˈseɪm ˈpeɪdʒ].
commonMistakes: Saying 'flexible' with the stress on the second syllable

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a diplomatic suggestion.
quests.hint: 'respect' stresses SPECT, 'suggest' stresses JEST, and 'committing' stresses MIT.
quests.explanation: 'With respect' is a formal softener: quick and light. The suggestion carries the peaks: sugGEST, TEST, SMALLer scale, beFORE, WHOLE.
quests.textToSpeak: With respect, I'd suggest we test the idea on a smaller scale before committing the whole budget.
quests.phoneticHint: [wɪð rɪˈspekt aɪd səˈdʒest wi ˈtest ði aɪˈdɪə ɒn ə ˈsmɔːlər ˈskeɪl bɪˈfɔːr kəˈmɪtɪŋ ðə ˈhoʊl ˈbʌdʒɪt].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as you present a slide.
quests.hint: 'increased' is inCREASED, 'steadily' stresses STEAD, and 'throughout' stresses OUT.
quests.explanation: A signpost like 'as you can see' is quick and light. Then the main message: SALES inCREASED STEADily.
quests.textToSpeak: As you can see on this slide, sales increased steadily throughout the year.
quests.phoneticHint: [əz jə kən ˈsiː ɒn ðɪs ˈslaɪd] | [ˈseɪlz ɪnˈkriːst ˈstedɪli θruːˈaʊt ðə ˈjɪr].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as you present a chart.
quests.hint: 'compares' stresses PARES, 'three' has [θr], and 'successful' stresses CESS.
quests.explanation: Comparing options needs a rhythm: list the options, then highlight the best. The blue line and MOST successful take the extra stress.
quests.textToSpeak: This graph compares three different approaches; the blue line shows the most successful one.
quests.phoneticHint: [ðɪs ˈgræf kəmˈpeərz ˈθriː ˈdɪfrənt əˈproʊtʃɪz] | [ðə ˈbluː ˈlaɪn ˈʃoʊz ðə ˈmoʊst səkˈsesfəl ˈwʌn].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as you highlight a key point.
quests.hint: 'interesting' is IN-tres-ting, 'sudden' stresses SUD, and 'March' ends in [tʃ].
quests.explanation: Pointing out a key feature: pause after 'here', then stress SUDden DROP. 'which we'll come back to' is a quick aside.
quests.textToSpeak: What's interesting here is the sudden drop in March, which we'll come back to in a moment.
quests.phoneticHint: [ˈwɒts ˈɪntrəstɪŋ ˈhɪr ɪz ðə ˈsʌdən ˈdrɒp ɪn ˈmɑːrtʃ] | [wɪtʃ wiːl ˈkʌm ˈbæk tə ɪn ə ˈmoʊmənt].
commonMistakes: Giving 'interesting' the stress on the second syllable

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a reply in a Q&A.
quests.hint: 'great question' peaks on GREAT and QUES; 'let me think' is a light filler.
quests.explanation: A stalling phrase buys time. Keep it slow and warm: rise on 'question', then steady on the explanation.
quests.textToSpeak: That's a great question; let me think about how best to explain it.
quests.phoneticHint: [ðæts ə ˈgreɪt ˈkwestʃən] | [let mi ˈθɪŋk əˈbaʊt haʊ ˈbest tu ɪkˈspleɪn ɪt].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a Q&A answer.
quests.hint: 'exact' is ig-ZAKT, 'figures' stresses FIG, and 'follow up' peaks on UP.
quests.explanation: Admitting a limit: use a small fall-rise on 'me', then a firm fall on 'session'. 'exact' has [gz], not [ks].
quests.textToSpeak: I don't have the exact figures with me, but I'll follow up by email after the session.
quests.phoneticHint: [aɪ ˈdoʊnt həv ði ɪgˈzækt ˈfɪgjərz wɪð ˈmiː] | [bət aɪl ˈfɒloʊ ˈʌp baɪ ˈiːmeɪl ˈæftər ðə ˈseʃən].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as you would check a question.
quests.hint: 'understand' stresses STAND, 'correctly' stresses RECT, and 'sample' has [mp].
quests.explanation: Rephrasing a question: slow and rising on the key idea, then a fall. 'whether the results' runs together as 'whether-the-results'.
quests.textToSpeak: If I understand correctly, you're asking whether the results would change with a larger sample.
quests.phoneticHint: [ɪf aɪ ˌʌndərˈstænd kəˈrektli] | [jɔːr ˈæskɪŋ ˈweðər ðə rɪˈzʌlts wʊd ˈtʃeɪndʒ wɪð ə ˈlɑːrdʒər ˈsæmpəl].
commonMistakes: Saying 'sample' as 'sam-pull' with a strong final vowel

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a friendly customer-service greeting.
quests.hint: 'Good afternoon' has a fall on NOON; 'thank you for calling' is quick; 'How can I help you' rises on HELP.
quests.explanation: A greeting is warm: start slightly higher, keep a smile in the voice, and use a gentle rise on 'today'.
quests.textToSpeak: Good afternoon, and thank you for calling. How can I help you today?
quests.targetPhoneme: customer service greeting: warmth and stress
quests.phoneticHint: [ˈgʊd ˌæftərˈnuːn ən ˈθæŋk jə fə ˈkɔːlɪŋ] | [ˈhaʊ kən aɪ ˈhelp jə təˈdeɪ] rising.
commonMistakes: Saying 'thank you for' as heavy words
Using a low, flat tone, which sounds unwelcoming

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud with empathy.
quests.hint: Empathy lives on 'so', 'frustrating' and 'completely'; 'let me see' is soft.
quests.explanation: To sound sincere, add pitch on the emotion words and slow down slightly. 'frustrating' has [str] and stress on the first syllable.
quests.textToSpeak: That must be so frustrating; I completely understand, and let me see what I can do.
quests.phoneticHint: [ðæt məst bi ˈsoʊ ˈfrʌstreɪtɪŋ] | [aɪ kəmˈpliːtli ˌʌndərˈstænd] | [ənd ˈlet mi ˈsiː wɒt aɪ kən ˈduː].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as you explain a finding.
quests.hint: 'processed' ends in [st], 'twice' has [tw], and 'mistake' stresses STAKE.
quests.explanation: Explaining a finding: state the check, then the result. 'processed twice' links as 'processed-twice' with an [st]+[tw] cluster.
quests.textToSpeak: I've checked your account, and it looks like the payment was processed twice by mistake.
quests.phoneticHint: [aɪv ˈtʃekt jər əˈkaʊnt] | [ənd ɪt ˈlʊks ˈlaɪk ðə ˈpeɪmənt wəz ˈprɒsest ˈtwaɪs baɪ mɪˈsteɪk].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a sincere apology.
quests.hint: 'inconvenience' stresses VEEN, 'arrange' stresses RANGE, and 'replacement' stresses PLACE.
quests.explanation: An apology should sound sincere: slow slightly on 'sorry' and 'inconvenience'. 'arrange' has [dʒ] at the end.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm sorry for the inconvenience; I'll arrange a replacement for you straight away.
quests.phoneticHint: [aɪm ˈsɒri fə ði ˌɪnkənˈviːniəns] | [aɪl əˈreɪndʒ ə rɪˈpleɪsmənt fə ju ˈstreɪt əˈweɪ].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a calm complaint.
quests.hint: 'damaged' ends in [dʒd], 'refund' as a noun stresses REE, and 'full' has [ʊ].
quests.explanation: A clear complaint is calm and firm. 'damaged' has two syllables (DAM-ijd) and ends with [dʒd].
quests.textToSpeak: The item arrived damaged, so I'd like a full refund, please.
quests.phoneticHint: [ði ˈaɪtəm əˈraɪvd ˈdæmɪdʒd] | [soʊ aɪd ˈlaɪk ə ˈfʊl ˈriːfʌnd pliːz].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a customer-service explanation.
quests.hint: 'unfortunately' stresses FOR, 'appear' stresses PEAR, and 'statement' stresses STATE.
quests.explanation: Explaining a delay: a softener, then facts. Numbers and time phrases carry the peaks: UP TO FIVE WORKing DAYS.
quests.textToSpeak: Unfortunately, the refund can take up to five working days to appear on your statement.
quests.phoneticHint: [ʌnˈfɔːrtʃənətli ðə ˈriːfʌnd kən ˈteɪk ˈʌp tə ˈfaɪv ˈwɜːrkɪŋ ˈdeɪz tu əˈpɪr ɒn jər ˈsteɪtmənt].
commonMistakes: Putting the main stress on 'ly' in 'unfortunately'
Saying 'appear' with the stress on the first syllable
